source_caption:
In the movie, Kakihara is a handsome young man with a slender, athletic build, wearing flashy leisure suits with long satin jackets and coats. In the manga, he was originally depicted as a creepy-looking, middle-aged man with an average, hairy build, wearing a black two-piece suit, a black tie, and shibari ropes as undergarments. His countless piercings, facial scars, and stylish shoes were some of the few characteristics that remained unchanged in the film.

The marks on the sides of Kakihara’s mouth are known as a Glasgow smile or Chelsea smile. The film’s color cover is a mirror image of his face, with the cross over his right eye, while the black-and-white cover shows it over his left eye, as seen in the film.

Dir. Takashi Miike

source_details.title: Ichi the Killer
source_details.synopsis: Ichi the Killer (Japanese: 殺し屋1, romanized: Koroshiya Ichi, lit. 'Hitman One') is a 2001 Japanese yakuza splatter film directed by Takashi Miike, written by Sakichi Sato, and starring Tadanobu Asano and Nao Omori. Based on Hideo Yamamoto's manga series of the same name, its plot follows a psychologically damaged man who is manipulated into assaulting or killing rival faction members of feuding yakuza gangs while being pursued by a sadomasochistic enforcer. The film has garnered controversy due to its graphic depictions of violence and cruelty and was subject to censorship in several countries.
